final_answer: The Rosetta Stone holds immense significance as a pivotal artifact in the study of ancient Egypt. It features the same text inscribed in three scripts: Ancient Greek, Demotic, and Egyptian hieroglyphics. This trilingual format provided scholars with a critical tool for deciphering hieroglyphics, as the Greek text was already understood. By comparing the Greek script with the hieroglyphic and Demotic versions, scholars could identify phonetic correspondences and symbolic meanings within the hieroglyphic script. Jean-François Champollion, leveraging his knowledge of Coptic, a descendant of the Egyptian language, was able to unlock the phonetic and symbolic elements of hieroglyphics, thereby enabling the modern understanding of ancient Egyptian language and culture. The Rosetta Stone thus served as the key to unlocking a previously indecipherable script, revolutionizing the study of ancient Egypt.
